arxiv-2005-12081.title: Two cultures: “them and us” in the academic world
arxiv-2005-12081.creator: R. Kenna ? , ?
arxiv-2005-12081.description: Abstract Impact of academic research onto the non-academic world is of increasing importance as authorities seek return on public investment. Impact opens new opportunities for what are known as ‘‘professional services’’: as scientometrical tools bestow some with confidence they can quantify quality, the impact agenda brings lay measurements to evaluation of research.

arxiv-2105-00744.title: A remark on the quasilocal calculation of tidal heating: energy transfer through the quasilocal surface
arxiv-2105-00744.creator: Albert Huber
arxiv-2105-00744.description: Abstract In this note, using the quasilocal formalism of Brown and York, the flow of energy through a closed surface containing a gravitating physical system is calculated in a way that augments earlier results on the subject by Booth and Creighton.

arxiv-2309-12253.title: SALSA-CLRS: A Sparse and Scalable Benchmark for Algorithmic Reasoning
arxiv-2309-12253.creator: Julian Minder, Florian Grötschla, Joël Mathys, Roger Wattenhofer
arxiv-2309-12253.description: Abstract We introduce an extension to the CLRS algorithmic learning benchmark, prioritizing scalability and the utilization of sparse representations. Many algorithms in CLRS require global memory or information exchange, mirrored in its execution model, which constructs fully connected ( not sparse ) graphs based on the underlying problem.

arxiv-2404-07521.title: Advancements in Secondary and Backscattered Electron Energy Spectra and Yields Analysis: from Theory to Applications
arxiv-2404-07521.creator: Simone Taioli, Maurizio Dapor
arxiv-2404-07521.description: Abstract Over the past decade, experimental microscopy and spectroscopy have made significant progress in the study of the morphological, optical, electronic and transport properties of materials. These developments include higher spatial resolution, shorter acquisition times, more efficient monochromators and electron analysers, improved contrast imaging and advancements in sample preparation techniques.

arxiv-2405-18681.title: A random-key GRASP for combinatorial optimization
arxiv-2405-18681.creator: A.A. Chaves 1,∗ , M.G.C. Resende 1,2 , R.M.A. Silva 3
arxiv-2405-18681.description: Abstract 1 Departamento de Ciência e Tecnologia, Universidade Federal de São Paulo, São José dos Campos, SP, Brazil 2 Industrial and Systems Engineering, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, U.S.A. 3 Centro de Informática, Universidade Federal de Pernambuco, Recife, PE, Brazil Abstract. arxiv-2407-00826.title: NAIST Simultaneous Speech Translation System for IWSLT 2024
arxiv-2407-00826.creator: Yuka Ko, Ryo Fukuda, Yuta Nishikawa, Yasumasa Kano, Tomoya Yanagita
arxiv-2407-00826.description: Abstract This paper describes NAIST’s submission to the simultaneous track of the IWSLT 2024 Evaluation Campaign: English-to-{German, Japanese, Chinese} speech-to-text translation and English-to-Japanese speech-to-speech translation. We develop a multilingual end-to-end speech-to-text translation model combining two pre-trained language models, HuBERT and mBART. We trained this model with two decoding policies, Local Agreement (LA) and AlignAtt.

arxiv-2507-03835.title: Confinement/deconfinement at low temperatures and rotation in the exact soft wall model
arxiv-2507-03835.creator: Octavio C. Junqueira, Roldao da Rocha
arxiv-2507-03835.description: Abstract We study the effects of rotation on the confinement/deconfinement phase transition of strongly interacting matter, at low temperatures, in the soft wall AdS/QCD model at finite density. To achieve it, we apply the Hawking-Page approach to the exact Andreev’s solution of a charged rotating black hole in five-dimensional AdS space.

britannica-1911-conscience-hendrik.description: Article 'Conscience, Hendrik' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 6), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. born at Antwerp on the 3rd of December 1812. Although he invariably signed his name Hendrik, his baptismal name was Henri. He was the son of a Frenchman, Pierre Conscience, from Besançon, who had been chef de timonerie in the navy of Napoleon, and who was appointed under-harbourmaster at Antwerp in 1811, when that city formed part of France.

pmc-10550742.creator: Norlisah Mohd Ramli, Norzaini Rose Mohd Zain
pmc-10550742.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). d Singapore (6.6:100000) have significantly higher percentages of radiologists in the population [2]. This brief article updates Malaysia’s unique healthcare model, the current distribution of radiological premises, the need for more radiologists and potential solutions to address this shortage. Healthcare Model in Malaysia Malaysia’s healthcare system combines government-provided services such as those provided by the Ministry of Health (MOH), Ministry of Defense, university-based (teaching hospitals), and private healthcare.

pmc-11468398.title: A participatory research to assess how a student citizens’ assembly can facilitate the co-creation of nutrition interventions in higher education settings
pmc-11468398.creator: Alice Bellicha, Benjamin Allès, Julia Baudry, Lucile Bouré, Henri Dehove, Hajar El Karmouni, Emilie Frenkiel, Emmanuelle Kesse-Guyot, Sandrine Péneau, Malo Mofakhami, the USPN Student Citizens’ Assembly Group
pmc-11468398.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe transition period from adolescence to early adulthood is critical for developing new nutritional behaviors, making higher education students an important target group for public health nutrition interventions. Given the complexity of nutrition-related behaviors and their various determinants, involving the student population (the future beneficiaries of interventions) and the partners engaged in their implementation when designing campus nutrition interventions is essential. Citizens’ assemblies are deliberative processes which are more and more frequently organized to co-create solutions to complex problems.

pmc-11510880.title: Serum Albumin in Nasal Drug Delivery Systems: Exploring the Role and Application
pmc-11510880.creator: Sandra Aulia Mardikasari, Gábor Katona, Ildikó Csóka
pmc-11510880.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The application of serum albumin in various types of formulations has emerged as a valuable option in biomedical research, especially in the field of nasal drug delivery systems. A serum albumin-based carrier system has been employed due to several benefits, such as enhancing drug solubility and stability, generating the desired controlled release profile, and developing favorable properties with respect to the challenges in nasal conditions, which, in this case, involves hindering rapid elimination due to nasal mucociliary clearance.

pmc-11607401.title: Y chromosome introgression between deeply divergent primate species
pmc-11607401.creator: Axel Jensen, Emma R Horton, Junior Amboko, Stacy-Anne Parke, John A Hart, Anthony J Tosi, Katerina Guschanski, Kate M Detwiler
pmc-11607401.description: Hybridization and introgression are widespread in nature, with important implications for adaptation and speciation. Since heterogametic hybrids often have lower fitness than homogametic individuals, a phenomenon known as Haldane’s rule, loci inherited strictly through the heterogametic sex rarely introgress. We focus on the Y-chromosomal history of guenons, African primates that hybridized extensively in the past.

pmc-11678641.title: Acetamiprid Exposure Disrupts Gut Microbiota in Adult and Larval Worker Honeybees (Apis mellifera L.)
pmc-11678641.creator: Yuchen Su, Jingliang Shi, Yueyang Hu, Jianhui Liu, Xiaobo Wu
pmc-11678641.description: Simple SummaryThe pesticide acetamiprid, widely used to protect outdoor crops, poses lesser risks to pollinators like honeybees compared to other pesticides. However, its impact on honeybees’ gut microbiota remains unclear. This study revealed that acetamiprid significantly altered the gut microbial community in both adult and larval bees, leading to disturbances in energy and neurometabolic pathways.

pmc-12707157.title: Resilience Factors and Their Association with Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms: An Intergenerational Perspective
pmc-12707157.creator: Adi Drapisz, Ron Walfisch, Tal Shilton, Nimrod Hertz-Palmor, Idit Dekel, Mariela Mosheva, Doron Gothelf, Ran Barzilay
pmc-12707157.description: BackgroundCharacterizing variability in youth mental health trajectories from risk to resilience is crucial for elucidating the heterogeneity present within clinical populations. Limited knowledge exists regarding the intergenerational associations of resilience factors. The present study aimed to examine the associations between resilience factors and psychopathology in youth referred for outpatient psychiatric evaluation and their parents.

pmc-12812705.creator: Sónia Dias Coelho, Diana Campos, Mónica Almeida, Carla Quintaneiro, Miguel Oliveira, Isabel Lopes
pmc-12812705.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The reduction in the number of animals being used in experimental assays has been a concern of the scientific community. In this sense, non-animal alternative methods have been increasingly tested. This study intended to explore how cell-based responses compare to organismal outcomes and if the former models could contribute to minimizing the number of live animals needed in subsequent stages of hazard/risk assessment of chemicals on amphibians.

pmc-13051891.title: Mad Honey Poisoning Presenting With Anaphylaxis and Cardiovascular Instability: A Case Series
pmc-13051891.creator: Abal Baral, Kusha K C, Kun Li
pmc-13051891.description: BackgroundMad honey differs from commercial honey due to contamination with grayanotoxins. These toxins are produced when honey bees extract nectar and pollen from various Rhododendron species. While cardiovascular toxicity is well‐documented, anaphylactic reactions are rare and underreported.Case PresentationThis case series describes seven patients presenting to a rural primary care hospital in Nepal between June 2024 and January 2025.

pmc-13264945.title: Safety and effectiveness of tocilizumab in systemic sclerosis: a multicentre French-Italian study
pmc-13264945.creator: Giulia Buonsante, Giacomo De Luca, Elena Marazzi, Fabio Cacciapaglia, Maria Grazia Lazzaroni, Marco De Pinto, Devis Benfaremo, Valentina Longo, Carlo Iandoli, Giovanna Cuomo, Anna Cuberli, Elisabetta Zanatta, Alain Lescoat, Silvia Bellando-Randone, Giorgia Trignani, Serena Guiducci, Lorenzo Beretta,
pmc-13264945.description: BackgroundTocilizumab (TCZ) has shown beneficial effects on interstitial lung disease (ILD) in systemic sclerosis (SSc). We aimed to assess the real-life safety and effectiveness of TCZ on several SSc-related domains using data from a French-Italian multicentre cohort.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective analysis of patients with SSc treated with TCZ across 15 referral centres.

pmc-13319986.title: Body Iron Stores and Metabolic Syndrome in Adults Free of Cardiometabolic Disease From Southwestern Colombia
pmc-13319986.creator: Milton Fabian Suárez-Ortegón, José Guillermo Ortega-Ávila, Diana María Caicedo-Borrero, Mildrey Mosquera
pmc-13319986.description: Evidence linking serum ferritin (SF) with metabolic syndrome (MetS) remains inconsistent by sex. Data from Latin American populations are lacking, and adults free of cardiometabolic disease remain understudied. We examined whether SF was independently associated with MetS (harmonized definition) in adults from Cali, Colombia.

pmc-13455437.title: Use of distal embolic protection devices as a bailout strategy for suboptimal flow reversal during transcarotid artery revascularization: illustrative case
pmc-13455437.creator: Andrew B Koo, Sasha Stogniy, Abdelaziz Amllay, Kshiraj V Talati, Daniela Renedo, Joseph Haynes, Joseph Antonios, Nanthiya Sujijantarat, Ryan Hebert, Charles C Matouk
pmc-13455437.description: BACKGROUNDTranscarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) has become an increasingly utilized surgical option for carotid disease, relying on flow reversal for distal embolic protection (DEP). However, anatomical variations, such as an isolated middle cerebral artery hemisphere, and severe carotid stenosis may compromise the safety of flow reversal intraoperatively.

pmc-13685188.title: Ileorectal fistula after resection of perforated sigmoid tumor and Hartmann’s procedure with uterine invasion: a case report
pmc-13685188.creator: Armin Ahmadi, Jalal Manoochehri, Khaled Rahmani
pmc-13685188.description: IntroductionGastrointestinal fistulas are rare but serious postoperative complications, particularly when arising between the ileum and rectum. They are typically associated with complex intra-abdominal surgeries, malignancies, or inflammatory conditions. This case report presents a rare instance of ileorectal fistula formation following resection of a perforated sigmoid tumor with uterine invasion and subsequent Hartmann's procedure.
